question.knowledge_point: Differentiating a General Exponential Function Using the Chain Rule
question.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f={3}^{u},\,u=2{x}^{2}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}={3}^{u}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3),\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={3}^{u}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)\cdot (4x) \\  & =4x\cdot {3}^{u}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\  & =4x\cdot {3}^{2{x}^{2}}\operatorname{ln}⁡(3).\end{aligned}
$$
